name: Pishe Pasha
description: Pishe Pasha is a two-player competitive patience game played in Jewish communities in North America since at least the mid-twentieth century. Each player has a face-down stock of 26 cards. Players get rid of cards by building foundation piles (Ace through King in each suit) or by playing onto the opponent's discard pile (next higher or lower rank). The first to empty their stock and discard wins.

history.origins: Played in America, primarily in Jewish communities, since at least the mid-twentieth century; presumably originated in Europe. Many slight variations and spellings exist (Pisha Pasha, Pisha Paysha, Persian Pasha).
timeline: Mid-twentieth century: Documented in North American Jewish communities
Ongoing: Played as a social and family game
history.cultural: Popular in Jewish communities in North America as a two-player social and family game.

setup.players: Usually two players (three possible; see variations). No partnerships.
setup.deck:
Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
setup.dealing: Cards shuffled; each player receives a stock of 26 cards face down. Traditionally the first cards are dealt two at a time, the remainder three at a time.

rules.objective: Get rid of all your cards by playing them to foundation piles (A-2-3-...-K in each suit) or onto your opponent's discard pile. The first to empty both stock and discard wins; the winner scores one point per card left in the opponent's stock and discard.
rules.gameplay: Non-dealer starts by turning the top card of her stock. If it is not an ace, she must discard it face up to start her discard pile and her turn ends. If it is an ace, she plays it to start that suit's foundation and continues turning stock cards, playing any that fit a foundation (ace or next higher in same suit), until one does not fit; that card is discarded and her turn ends. The dealer then plays: turn the top stock card; if it fits a foundation it must be played there; if it is one higher or one lower than the top of the opponent's discard (any suit) it may be played there. Continue turning stock and playing until an unplayable card is turned; discard it to your own pile and your turn ends. From each player's second turn onward, at any point you may also play the top card of your own discard pile to a foundation (mandatory if possible) or to the opponent's discard (optional). When you cannot or do not wish to play from discard, turn the next stock card and play as above. When stock is empty, turn your discard pile face down as a new stock. If you empty both stock and discard you win.
keyRules: Foundation piles build A-2-3-...-K in each suit in the center.
You may play onto the opponent's discard if your card is exactly one rank higher or lower (suit irrelevant).
If a player breaks the rules, opponent may call 'stop' and either force the correct play or end the offender's turn.
Missing a play to the opponent's pile is legal; once you discard to your own pile or turn a stock card, you cannot undo it.

strategy.basic: Follow the rules: play to foundations when possible, and consider when to play onto the opponent's discard.
strategy.intermediate: Try to place the highest cards possible on your opponent's discard pile; being left with kings in your stock is bad. Remember the order of cards in your face-down stock to decide when to stop laying off onto the opponent and turn a stock card instead.
strategy.advanced: Balance giving cards to the opponent (to clear your pile) against giving them playable sequences; use knowledge of your stock order to time when to draw.
tips: Place high cards on the opponent's discard when you can.
Remember the order of cards in your stock to plan when to turn instead of playing from discard.
Kings left in stock are a disadvantage.

variations.name: Stop rule
variations.description: Some play without the stop rule: a player who fails to play to a foundation can be forced to correct the mistake, but the turn continues.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule toggle only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Compulsory play on opponent's pile
variations.description: If at any point during your turn the card you draw or the top of your discard does not fit a foundation but does fit the opponent's discard, it must be played there. Calling 'Pishe Pasha' on opponent error ends their turn; you may transfer cards from your discard to theirs if they fit, and transfer the bottom three (or one/two in milder versions) of your stock to the bottom of theirs.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule variant; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Three-player game
variations.description: Each player has 17 cards; one face-up card starts a single center foundation built upward regardless of suit (continuing king to ace to two). Compulsory to play to center when possible; otherwise play next higher or lower on either opponent's discard, or discard to your own pile. Turn passes clockwise.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Player count and layout variant; would require engine constants for 3 players.

variations.name: Simple book version (Pisha Pasha)
variations.description: A simpler game of pure chance, similar to War: players divide the pack, turn top cards simultaneously; same suit the higher card takes the opponent's discard pile. First to collect all cards wins. Often documented in books under Pisha Pasha.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Different game; not the main competitive patience form.

scoring.description: Winner scores one point per card remaining in the opponent's stock and discard.
scoring.winCondition: First player to empty both stock and discard pile wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Pishe Pasha is a two-player competitive patience game: build foundation piles or play onto the opponent's discard; first to empty stock and discard wins.
